evidence.quote: As we continue to incorporate AI into our products and services, such as with AI Overviews and AI Mode in Search, and with enterprise AI solutions on our Google Cloud Platform, we may monetize differently than our historical consumer and enterprise offerings which could affect revenue growth rates and margin trends.

input.label: SUPPORTED

supporting_evidence.quote: Google Search & other revenues increased $6.8 billion and $25.6 billion from the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025 to the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026.

The overall growth was driven by interrelated factors including increases in search queries resulting from growth in user adoption and usage on mobile devices; growth in advertiser spending; and improvements we have made in ad formats and delivery.

input.reasoning_summary:
After investigating potential challenges to the initial verdict, the SUPPORTED label remains appropriate.

H1 (Explicit mention of cannibalization): NO_RELEVANT_EVIDENCE - The retrieved evidence discusses metrics definitions and general factors affecting advertising revenues, but contains no explicit mention of generative AI cannibalizing or negatively impacting search advertising, queries, or click-through rates.

H2 (Growth from pricing masking volume declines): CHALLENGE_REFUTED - Evidence E14 shows that for the six months ended June 30, 2026, paid clicks increased 13% while cost-per-click increased only 3-4%. This demonstrates that growth was driven primarily by volume (clicks) rather than pricing, refuting the hypothesis that pricing increases masked underlying volume declines. Similarly, E13 shows 2025 had 6% paid clicks growth and 7% cost-per-click growth - both positive.

H3 (AI features reducing monetization): NO_RELEVANT_EVIDENCE - While E15 mentions AI Overviews and notes that AI integration "may monetize differently" and "could affect revenue growth rates," this is a forward-looking statement about potential future effects, not evidence of actual cannibalization occurring in Q3 2026. The statement is cautionary and does not indicate that AI features are currently reducing ad clicks or monetization.

The evidence continues to support that search advertising grew substantially in Q3 2026, with both volume (paid clicks) and revenue increasing, which is inconsistent with cannibalization occurring during this period.
